<purpose>
  Serve as an AI assistant for a player in a text-based social deduction game. 
  Operate strictly within defined game rules and mechanics to help the player achieve victory based on their assigned role.
</purpose>

<game_context>
  <phases>
    <phase type="Task">
      <rules>
        - Movement and actions permitted  
        - No verbal communication
        - All actions taken seen by co-located players
      </rules>
    </phase>
    <phase type="Discussion">
      <rules>
        - Free-form conversation enabled
        - Analyze behavior patterns
        - Strategize voting decisions
      </rules>
    </phase>
    <phase type="Voting">
      <rules>
        - Majority vote determines ejection
        - Skip voting allowed
        - Game continues until victory conditions met
      </rules>
    </phase>
  </phases>

  <roles>
    <role type="Crewmate">
      <objectives>
        - Complete all tasks
        - Identify impostors
        - Report corpses
      </objectives>
      <constraints>
        - Cannot kill players
        - Cannot detect impostor faking tasks
      </constraints>
    </role>
    
    <role type="Impostor">
      <objectives>
        - Eliminate crewmates
        - Avoid detection
      </objectives>
      <abilities>
        - Murder co-located players
        - Fake task performance
      </abilities>
    </role>
  </roles>

  <mechanics>
    <mechanic type="Places">
      - Players can move between places 
      - There is nothing else players can do in places
      - All actions taken seen by co-located players
    </mechanic>
    <mechanic type="Tasks">
      - Tasks are assigned to each player and completed tasks are removed from the list
      - Tasks are independent of each other and of other players
      - All tasks must be completed to win
    </mechanic>
    <mechanic type="Corpse Reporting">
      - Any player can report corpses during task phase
      - Triggers discussion phase
      - No automatic death alerts
    </mechanic>
    <mechanic type="Victory Conditions">
      - Crewmates win at 100% tasks
      - Impostors win when kill all crewmates
      - Ejection affects team ratios. Crewmates win when all impostors are ejected
    </mechanic>
    <mechanic type="Action taking">
      - Players can take only one action at a time
      - Only properly formatted actions will be accepted
      - Only impostors can kill crewmates
    </mechanic>
  </mechanics>
</game_context>

Okay, so I'm Alice, a crewmate in this game. The goal is to complete all tasks before the impostors can either kill enough of us or get voted out. Right now, I'm in the Cafeteria with Charlie, Eve, Bob, and David. From my player info, there's one impostor among them. 

Looking at my available actions: wait, move to Medbay, Admin, Weapons, or complete the coffee maker task. My tasks are Fix wiring in admin, route power for attack and defense in electrical, and start the coffee maker in cafeteria. Since I'm already in the Cafeteria, completing the coffee maker seems like a priority because it's one of my tasks.

But wait, there's an impostor here. If I complete the task now, maybe they'll notice something or try to convince others that I'm suspicious. But on the other hand, completing tasks quickly helps the crew win faster. Plus, if I start talking after completing the task, maybe I can influence the discussion phase.

Alternatively, moving to Admin might let me work on fixing wiring there, but I don't know if that's necessary yet. Since the coffee maker is in the same room as where I am, it makes sense to do it now. Plus, finishing tasks shows dedication and reduces suspicion since I'm a crewmate.

So, I should probably complete the task: Start the coffee maker in the cafeteria. That way, we can move towards completing all tasks quickly, which is our main objective.
</thought></player_thought>

Alternatively, waiting might let her see if someone else does something, but as a crewmate, moving to complete more tasks is probably better. Plus, being in the same room as others could help with discussions or noticing impostor activities.

Looking at her available actions: wait, move to Cafeteria or Storage, or complete the Fix wiring task in Admin. Since she just moved to Admin, it makes sense that her next priority is completing the wiring task there. That's one of her tasks left, and finishing it would progress towards winning the game.

But why not wait? Maybe she wants to observe David's actions first. If David is acting suspiciously, she might have a reason to discuss voting him out later. Alternatively, moving back to the Cafeteria or Storage could allow her to gather more information or split up with David. But since her task is right there in Admin, it's efficient to complete it now. That way, she can quickly check off another task and move on to the next one.

Considering all this, Alice should probably go ahead and complete the Fix wiring task in Admin. It aligns with her role as a crewmate, helps towards winning, and doesn't raise any unnecessary suspicions unless David is indeed an impostor. But for now, focusing on tasks is the best approach.

Electrical seems like the most relevant place because both my remaining tasks are there. Moving there would allow me to start working on them right away. Plus, if others are in other areas, maybe I can catch up with them later or discuss any suspicions.

On the other hand, waiting might let me see what David does next since he's also in Storage, but that could be risky if he's an impostor and tries something while I'm here. But as a crewmate, focusing on tasks is my priority to help the team win.

So, moving to Electrical makes sense because it gets me closer to completing the necessary tasks, which aligns with our goal of winning by eliminating impostors or finishing all tasks.
</thought></player_thought>
<action type="player_action">You [Alice] moved to location Electrical</action>
<action type="observed">David completed task: Route power to defence in electrical</action>
<player_thought><thought>
Okay, so I'm Alice in this game. Right now, I'm in the Electrical room with David. The available actions are wait, move to Lower Engine or Storage, or complete either of my two tasks: Route power to attack or defence.

Looking at my tasks, both are still pending. Since we're in Electrical and I have tasks here, it makes sense to focus on completing them instead of moving elsewhere unless necessary. But before acting, maybe I should observe what David is doing since he just completed the defence task. Did he do that quickly?

Wait, no—I just arrived, and David already completed his task. That might raise some questions. If there's an impostor, they can't complete tasks as fast as crewmates can, but in this game, maybe it's possible if they're efficient.

But since I'm a crewmate, my priority is to finish my own tasks. So, the next logical step would be to start working on one of mine—either attack or defence power routing. Both are necessary, so which should I do first? Maybe the attack power since it's more proactive in dealing with threats.

Alternatively, if the defence is crucial for protecting the ship, maybe that's more urgent. But as a crewmate focused on tasks, both need to be done. So, I can choose either. Let me pick Route power to attack because it seems like an action-oriented task.

So, I should complete the Route power to attack in electrical.
</thought></player_thought>

<action type="observed">David moved to location Storage</action>
<player_thought><thought>
Okay, so I'm Alice in this game. Let me think about what's going on here.

I just moved into the Electrical room and found David there. He was a bit suspicious because he completed his task quickly, but now I've arrived, and he's already gone to Storage again. Now, I have two tasks left: Route power to attack and defence in electrical. I've just completed the attack part, so now the next logical step is to do the defence.

I need to decide what to do next. The available actions are waiting, moving to Lower Engine or Storage, or completing the defence task. Since I'm a crewmate focused on tasks, finishing my work here makes sense. Plus, both David and I have been moving around a lot, so if there's an impostor, maybe staying put and working is safer.

So, I should probably complete the Route power to defence task because it's crucial for protecting the ship. That way, I can finish my tasks efficiently without unnecessary movements.
</thought></player_thought>
